_comment: NORMATIVE fixtures for endpoint metadata (platform / version / capabilities) and for
THE CENTRAL RULE, restated because it is the one that is easy to get wrong:
Capabilities are DESCRIPTIVE. Permissions are AUTHORITATIVE.
A peer advertising 'power.shutdown' has told you it owns a shutdown button. It has NOT
told you it may press yours. Only a grant permission may authorise an action, and the
grant is evaluated locally by the host that will execute the action — never by the
broker, and never from the peer's own advertisement.

metaVectors.name: a full Windows host advertisement
metaVectors._note: capabilities are returned sorted and de-duplicated so equality checks are stable across languages

metaVectors.name: a legacy Android client that predates this schema and sends no meta at all
metaVectors._note: MUST be accepted. Absent meta is not an error; it means 'unknown', and the UI must degrade to showing no capability-gated affordances rather than refusing the peer.

metaVectors.name: unknown capability tokens are dropped, not rejected
metaVectors._note: Forward compatibility: a newer peer advertising capabilities we have never heard of must still connect.

metaVectors.name: non-string capability entries are dropped without failing the whole meta
oversized capability list is truncated to the limit rather than rejected
metaVectors._note: GENERATE:64 means the test harness synthesises 64 distinct unknown tokens. All are unknown, so all are dropped; the point of the vector is that a 64-entry list must not blow up or be stored verbatim.

metaVectors.name: missing version defaults to unknown rather than failing

_rule: The shipped Android GrantStore uses enum Scope { VIEW, CONTROL, FILES, CLIPBOARD } and
serialises it as a 'scope' array. v1 grants use a 'permissions' array of the tokens above.
A grant carrying only legacy 'scope' MUST be widened through this table; a grant carrying
'permissions' uses them directly and 'scope' is ignored.
CRITICAL, and the reason this table is a fixture rather than a comment: no legacy scope maps
to any system.* permission. Every grant created before power control existed therefore confers
NO power over the machine. Fail closed on upgrade — an old grant must never silently acquire
the ability to shut down a PC.

vectors._note: CONTROL implies VIEW: controlling a screen you cannot see is not a coherent grant
reserved token; no Techee implementation acts on it
unknown legacy scope names are dropped, never guessed at

permissionRequiredFor._rule: Which grant permission each v1 control message requires before a host may execute it. A message whose permission is absent from the grant MUST be discarded and audited as PROTOCOL_REJECTION, not executed.

grantVectors.name: a screen-control grant does NOT imply shutdown
expiresAt exactly equal to now is still valid (expiry is strictly-less-than)
expiresAt of 0 means expired at the epoch, NOT 'never expires' — a truthiness guard on this field reads 0 as never-expiring and fails open
a legacy scope-only grant is widened, and confers no system power
a grant with neither permissions nor scope permits nothing
unknown permission tokens in a grant are dropped rather than honoured
